findings.problem: The duplicate protocol is a lookup followed by independent store and identity writes, with no atomic claim, lock, or recovery sequence. Two concurrent invocations can both see no hash owner and file separate live books. An interruption after filing a payload but before registering its hash can likewise make a later invocation miss the existing book. This violates the promised content-hash duplicate rule.
findings.suggestion: Specify an atomic hash reservation/claim (or a capture-wide lock) before creating a book, plus resume/rollback behavior for every interruption point; add parallel-capture and interruption/restart tests.

summary: The plan needs a crash- and concurrency-safe identity-claim design before it can reliably meet its no-duplicate completion criterion.
